title: Annotatio III open §.I: Transsubstantiation — if not by name, by rem older than Consubstantiation; absurd rem, late apt term
pass_a_gloss: ANNOTATIO III. On Transsubstantiation (to p. 36 at the end). A little Compendium embracing the History of Transsubstantiation. §. I. Transsubstantiation, if not as name, certainly as thing, is older than Consubstantiation; it exhibits the most absurd thing it designates, expressed by a term apt enough though invented quite late, at least as to the generic concept.
pass_b_english: Annotatio III opens on Transsubstantiation (to p. 36 end): a short History-compendium.
§.I: as rem (if not yet as name) it is older than Consubstantiation; the rem it names is most absurd; the term itself came late but fits the generic concept.
source_text: ANNOTATIO III. De Transsubstantiatione ad pag. 36. in fine. Historia Transsubstantiationis Compendiolum complexa. §. I. Transsubstantiatio, si non quà nomen, certè quà rem, Consubstantiatione antiquior, rem absurdissimam, quam designat, apto satis, etsi serò admodum invento terminô, quà genericum saltem conceptum, expressam exhibet.

choices.english: as / in respect of the thing
choices.why: older than Consubst. as rem not name
rejected: by the rem of a lawsuit

notes: Ann. III open; Transsubst. rem older than Consubst.
